howto.name: Add the PDF
howto.text: Drop or select the PDF you want to divide, up to 500 MB.

howto.name: Choose how to split
howto.text: By page ranges (the default) pulls the pages you list into one new PDF. Every page gives each page its own file. Every N pages cuts the document into equal chunks of the size you set.

howto.name: Enter pages or a chunk size
howto.text: For page ranges, type something like 1-3, 5, 7-end. For every N pages, enter the number of pages per part; the last part holds whatever remains.

howto.name: Split and download
howto.text: Run the split. Page ranges return a single PDF; the other two modes return a ZIP with one PDF per part.

faq.q: Which split mode should I use?
faq.a: Use page ranges to pull a specific set of pages into one file, Every page to break a document into single pages, and Every N pages to cut a long file into equal parts, for example separating a batch of two-page forms scanned together.

faq.q: How do I write page ranges?
faq.a: Pages are written as numbers and ranges separated by commas, such as 1-3, 5, 8-end; an open range like 4- runs to the last page. Page 0, pages beyond the end, and ranges written backwards are rejected with a message rather than guessed at.

faq.q: Why did I get one PDF instead of several?
faq.a: Because page ranges collects everything you list into a single document. To get separate files, choose Every page or Every N pages, which return a ZIP.
No. The split writes new files from a copy, and the PDF on your device stays exactly as it was.

faq.q: Can I split by bookmarks, file size or a word?
faq.a: Yes, with the dedicated tools: Split by Bookmarks cuts at each chapter, Split by Size cuts by a maximum file size you set, and Split by Text starts a new part at each page where a phrase appears.

faq.q: What happens to my PDF after I upload it?
faq.a: It is uploaded over HTTPS and split on the PrivaTools server in isolated temporary per-request storage, using local libraries rather than a third-party service. Response cleanup removes the PDF and the result after your download is sent, and a background sweep clears anything an interrupted request leaves behind. Nothing is added to an account or file library.
